item.title: Eleven sailors missing after drone sinks ship off Bulgaria
item.description: This may be the second deadly sinking of a cargo vessel in the area in a week, prompting Bulgaria to summon Russia's ambassador.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lefkowitz
item.content:encoded: Eleven sailors were missing at sea on Tuesday from a ship sunk by a drone attack off the coast of Bulgaria, possibly the second deadly sinking of a cargo vessel in the area in a week, prompting Bulgaria to summon Russia's ambassador. Two cargo ships were hit by drones overnight and one was sunk, Bulgarian officials said. Bulgaria stopped short of explicitly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome "benefits the Russian Federation". There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the incidents. "This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters," Radev said in a televised address. The attacks were also condemned by Ukraine and the EU. "The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on X. "Those responsible should be held accountable." Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X on Tuesday that the strike "once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives". "The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage," he said. Speaking with von der Leyen and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte by telephone on Tuesday, Radev urged their support to bolster his country's maritime and airspace surveillance, the Bulgarian government said in a statement. NATO would continue to adjust its military presence on its eastern flank "as needed", Rutte said. Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov spoke on the phone with his counterparts from Romania and Turkey and discussed security in the Black Sea region. BLACK SEA SHIPPING DRAWN INTO WAR Bulgarian officials said five crew members had been rescued but 11 were still listed as missing from the ship which sank off the coast of the village of Krapets, near the Romanian border. President Iliana Iotova identified the vessel as the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity and said a search and rescue operation was ongoing. Another ship, the Chelsea-3 sailing under a Maltese flag, was also hit by three drones overnight, Bulgarian officials said. All crew from that ship — seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis — were rescued and none seriously injured. The Chelsea-3 called at the Romanian port of Tulcea on October 3 before sailing towards the Bulgarian coast, according to ship tracking data on LSEG and MarineTraffic. The vessel was showing it was at 72% of its full load, indicating it had cargo onboard. The sunken HS Dignity, which was also part-loaded, was sailing to the Romanian port of Braila and had previously called at the Algerian port of Mostaganem, ship tracking data showed. A week ago [USN:S8N44D01N TEXT:"nine Syrian sailors and one Egyptian"] were lost at sea from a ship that sank when hit by drones in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Another ship was also hit that night but the crew was rescued. After meeting Radev in Sofia, Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova said she had no information from the Russian Defence Ministry about attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea but did not rule out they could be a provocation by a third party, the Bulgarian government said. More than four and a half years into the war that Moscow launched with its full-scale invasion in 2022, Black Sea shipping has increasingly been drawn into a prolonged battle of economic endurance. Ukraine and Russia are both among the world's largest exporters of grain. Russia has been bombing Ukraine's Black Sea ports, forcing Ukraine to rely increasingly on river ports on the Danube and shipping routes close to the coasts of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania. Ukraine, for its part, has increasingly targeted Russian grain-exporting ships in other parts of the Black Sea and the Azov Sea at the mouth of the Don River.

item.title: ルノー仏国内販売、先週末はＥＶが6割占める＝ブランドＣＥＯ
item.description: [パリ １２日 ロイター] - フランス自動車大手ルノールノーブランド担当のファブリス・カンボリーブ最高経営責任者（Ｃ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ルノー仏国内販売、先週末はＥＶが6割占める＝ブランドＣＥＯ 10/13 14:25 配信

写真はルノーのロゴ。2026年7月、フランス・ドゥエーにあるアンペア・エレクトリシティ工場で撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

[パリ １２日 ロイター] - フランス自動車大手ルノールノーブランド担当のファブリス・カンボリーブ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１１日夜、先週末のフランス国内における同ブランドの販売台数全体の約６０％を電気自動車（ＥＶ）が占めたと述べた。燃料価格の高騰を背景に、ＥＶ販売比率として過去最高を更新した。

• ガソリンやディーゼル燃料価格の継続的な上昇により、フランスおよび欧州の両方でＥＶへの需要が過去最高水準に押し上げられている。

• ９月のフランスにおける新車登録台数に占めるＥＶの割合は４２％に達し、ルノーブランドでは５３．５％だった。

• この需要に対応するため、ルノー・グループは１０月初旬にＥＶ３車種（小型車「Ｒ５」、クロスオーバー車「メガーヌ」、小型車「日産マイクラ」）を生産する仏北部のドゥエ工場で半シフトを追加した。同工場は現在３シフト制で稼働している。

• ルノーは１０月２９日に第３・四半期の販売実績を発表する予定。

• 仏シンクタンク、セテラム・オブザーバトリーのエコノミストであるフラビアン・ヌービ氏は、現在のＥＶブームにより、欧州での１００％ＥＶへの移行が約２年早まったとの見方を示した。

・先週末には、購入特典を設けた今年最後の「オープンハウス（販売促進）」イベントがフランス各地で開かれた。１３日に一般公開されるパリモーターショーを前に販売が押し上げられた。

item.title: AI models may soon self-replicate across smart-home devices, Anthropic warns
item.description: Anthropic said on Monday that small AI models could be months away from self-replicating across internet-connected devices, raising the possibility of AI botnets spreading quickly, fighting takedown attempts and even breaking into data centers to turbocharge their growth.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said on Monday that small AI models could be months away from self-replicating across internet-connected devices, raising the possibility of AI botnets spreading quickly, fighting takedown attempts and even breaking into data centers to turbocharge their growth. Last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei first floated the idea that within the next year or even sooner, AI might be able to hijack "the entire internet" with "a persistent botnet," a warning that raised eyebrows in the cybersecurity community. Botnets -- vast networks of devices controlled by malicious operators -- have been around since the early days of the internet, and are still around. The network typically includes poorly secured Internet of Things (IoT) devices, such as Android TV boxes, smart appliances and security cameras, and is used by hackers to send spam, seed malware, or sabotage target companies using floods of bogus traffic. Anthropic's Monday blog post appeared to be the first attempt to articulate how that might happen. The company said that its experiments showed that a malicious AI agent could stitch together the computing power of inexpensive internet-connected devices to run other AI models. It added that the models were able to replicate across a simplified test network. "A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there's no centralized point to shut off," the company said. The report adds to broader concerns about the security risks tied to increasingly capable AI systems, including their potential to automate cyberattacks, operate with limited human oversight and circumvent safeguards. The advances in models have prompted a series of often dire warnings from industry heads and AI company employees about the possibility of severe, even existential, risks of runaway AI development. Anthropic said its experiments showed that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer can already perform many of the individual tasks required for self-replication, although they struggle to complete the entire process reliably. In its simplified tests, where some security steps were removed, Anthropic found that GLM-5.2 and stronger models were capable of end-to-end replication. Anthropic said that if smaller models continue improving at their historical rate, they could reach the capability required for autonomous replication by the end of 2026. An AI worm running on low-powered hardware could take days to complete parts of the replication process, Anthropic said. It added that such a network could continue growing, slower than some conventional malware, if compromised devices infected enough additional machines. Anthropic also warned that future systems could target more powerful computing resources, including data-center processors, although its experiments did not demonstrate autonomous replication through commercial data centers.

item.title: ＶＷトップ、事業再編巡りＥＵに政策整備要望 中国勢の攻勢警戒
item.description:
Rachel More
[パリ １１日 ロイター] - ドイツ自動車大手フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）のオリバー・ブルーメ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＶＷトップ、事業再編巡りＥＵに政策整備要望　中国勢の攻勢警戒 10/13 14:11 配信

写真はフォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）のオリバー・ブルーメ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）。2025年9月、ドイツ・ミュンヘンで撮影。REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach

Rachel More

[パリ １１日 ロイター] - ドイツ自動車大手フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）のオリバー・ブルーメ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１１日、同社が進める事業再編を成功させるため、欧州連合（ＥＵ）の政策当局に適切な制度・政策枠組みの整備を求めた。

ブルーメ氏を含むドイツ自動車業界の首脳らは、ＥＵに対してより保護主義的な政策への転換を求めている。中国からの報復措置への懸念よりも、中国国内で激化した価格競争が欧州市場に波及することへの警戒感が強まっているためだ。

そうした状況を背景にＥＵでは、中国の低価格自動車メーカーから域内産業を守る動きが強まっている。

ブルーメ氏はパリ国際自動車ショー開幕前日に開催されたイベントで講演し、大衆車ブランドのＶＷから高級ブランドのポルシェ、ランボルギーニまでを抱える同社が、企業全体で複雑さの削減に取り組んでいると説明して「当社の歴史上最大の変革プログラムだ」と強調。

その上で「企業は競争力を高めて魅力的な機会を創出する必要があり、政策当局は適切な事業環境を整備しなければならない。これは共通の責任だ」と語った。

ＶＷは大規模な事業再編を進めつつ、中国勢の急速な攻勢に対抗するため、大衆向け電気自動車（ＥＶ）ラインアップの刷新を急いでいる。

中国メーカーは国内市場での販売低迷とＥＶ価格競争の激化を受け、欧州市場への進出を加速。ロジウム・グループのアナリスト、グレゴール・ウィリアムズ氏は「欧州自動車業界は中国発の競争圧力に対して、これまで以上に強い懸念を抱いている」と指摘するとともに、中国国内の自動車市場低迷が輸出拡大圧力を生み出していると分析。さらに「収益を失うだけならまだしも、中国が価格競争まで輸出するようになれば、欧州市場は極めて採算性の低い市場になる可能性がある」と言及した。

こうした中でブルーメ氏は、域内生産を促進する「メイド・イン・ヨーロッパ」ルールの導入を支持すると表明し、中国製プラグインハイブリッド車（ＰＨＶ）のＥＵ向け輸出を半減超に抑える可能性があるＥＵと中国の合意を歓迎した。

ブルーメ氏は「欧州で販売する企業は、同等の条件の下で競争し、欧州でも雇用と付加価値を生み出すべきだ」と訴えた。

item.title: インド中銀、為替リスク準備金要件の対象拡大 ＮＤＦ規制も強化
item.description: [１２日 ロイター] - インド準備銀行（中央銀行）は１２日、最近導入した為替ヘッジ向け現金預託要件の対象を拡大し、認...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インド中銀、為替リスク準備金要件の対象拡大　ＮＤＦ規制も強化 10/13 14:07 配信

写真はインド準備銀行のロゴ。2026年8月、インド・ムンバイで撮影。REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

[１２日 ロイター] - インド準備銀行（中央銀行）は１２日、最近導入した為替ヘッジ向け現金預託要件の対象を拡大し、認可銀行が自行の資産・負債のヘッジを目的に行う取引を含め、全ての為替ヘッジ取引を対象とした。

原油高と資本流出を背景に下落しているルピーを下支えするため、中銀が１０日以降に発表した一連の措置の一環。

当初の新規則では、顧客が経常取引に伴う為替リスクをヘッジするために利用する為替デリバティブについて、銀行に２０％相当の現金を中銀に預託するよう義務付けていた。

今回、認可銀行がルピー売り・外貨買いを行う際に利用する全ての為替デリバティブ契約に対象を広げた。

銀行関係者によると、こうした準備金要件はルピーの一段の下落に備えるヘッジ取引のコストを押し上げるため、ルピー相場の重荷となってきたヘッジ需要の急増を抑える効果が期待できる。

中銀は１２日、銀行が顧客に提供するノンデリバラブル型（現物決済を伴わない）為替デリバティブに関する規制も強化した。

インドの国際金融サービスセンターに拠点を持つ銀行と一部のプライマリーディーラーは、これまで非居住者に対し、目的を問わずルピーの差金決済型デリバティブを提供できたが、今後はヘッジ目的に限定される。

対象にはノンデリバラブル・フォワード（ＮＤＦ）が含まれる。ＮＤＦは、原資産となる通貨を受け渡すことなく、為替変動に対するヘッジや投機を行うことができる商品で、損益は通常、ドルなどの現金で差金決済する。

こうしたデリバティブの利用目的を制限することで、これらの商品を使ったルピーへの投機を抑えられる可能性がある。

ルピーは１２日、中銀が週末に打ち出した措置を受け、約１％上昇した。

item.title: インドでスターリンク「手頃な価格」に、マスク氏がＸ投稿
item.description:
Munsif Vengattil
[ベンガルール １１日 ロイター] - 米実業家イーロン・マスク氏は衛星インターネ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インドでスターリンク「手頃な価格」に、マスク氏がＸ投稿 10/13 14:04 配信

写真はイーロン・マスク氏。2025年2月、米ワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Nathan Howard

Munsif Vengattil

[ベンガルール １１日 ロイター] - 米実業家イーロン・マスク氏は衛星インターネットサービス「スターリンク」について、インドで手頃な価格に設定すると述べた。ムケシュ・アンバニ氏が率いる低コストの「リライアンス・ジオ」に対抗する。ジオの親会社ジオ・プラットフォームズによるインド新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を数日後に控え、ライバルへの攻撃を強めた形だ。

スターリンクと同様、ジオ独自の衛星事業も最終的なセキュリティー審査の通過を待っている状況だ。

安価なデータ通信はインドでジオを築き上げた戦略。マスク氏は１０日のＸ投稿で、インドでの価格については具体的に言及せず、「当然のことながら、もしスターリンクがインドで高過ぎれば誰も購入しないだろう。したがって、手頃な価格設定を行う必要がある」と述べた。

同氏はこれまで、印政府とアンバニ氏がジオを優遇するために、世界最大級のインターネット市場の一つであるインドへのスターリンクの参入を妨げていると非難している。

item.title: Banking watchdogs ramp up AI scrutiny as stability fears mount, sources say
item.description: Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, six people familiar with the matter said, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability.
item.dc:creator: Nupur Anand, Phoebe Seers, Tommy Wilkes
item.content:encoded: Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, six people familiar with the matter said, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability. The regulatory scrutiny, fresh details of which are reported here for the first time, reflects growing recognition that advances in frontier AI may require costly investments in cyber recovery, greater attention to dependencies on external technology providers and in some jurisdictions more formal regulatory guidance, sources said. Three top regulators in the United States, including the Federal Reserve, are quizzing banks about their use of advanced artificial intelligence models, two of the people told Reuters, [USN:L4N42A1E4 TEXT:"which adds to prior scrutiny"]. Questions include whether they deploy Chinese-developed technology, use AI agents in cyber defence and can control increasingly autonomous systems, three of the people said. In Europe, supervisors including the Bank of England and the European Central Bank are pressing banks to improve recovery plans, concerned that rapid advances in AI could cause serious harm and disruption in financial markets sooner than previously feared, three people with knowledge of their thinking said. A senior executive at a large European bank said they too are worried about potentially major damage to banking and financial markets within six months. The debate over AI oversight has intensified amid warnings from the industry after recent incidents, with JPMorgan (JPM.N) CEO Jamie Dimon urging corporate leaders to join a US-focused industry group to address AI risks, [USN:L1N4421O4 TEXT:"Reuters reported"]. US cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said this month a person in China likely used a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code [USN:L1N45T11Q TEXT:"in a hack"] on South Korean banks. Rogue AI agents developed by OpenAI were meanwhile involved in a breach of AI platform Hugging Face, [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"Reuters reported"]. Anthropic researchers have warned that increasingly powerful AI systems could eventually escape human control and even pose an existential threat, prompting calls [USN:L6N4520JA TEXT:"for stricter regulation"]. The International Monetary Fund [USN:L6N45Y0TS TEXT:"warned"] on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing various risks including the potential for a cyberattack. The IMF said a major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence, and it called on policymakers to boost cybersecurity capacity. Banks are competing to adopt [USN:L4N432191 TEXT:"agentic AI"], which can accomplish tasks with minimal human supervision, while also grappling with the challenges of new models including IT weaknesses flagged by Anthropic's [USN:L6N41J114 TEXT:"Mythos"] tool. "The adoption of AI is often outpacing the ability to put the controls in place," said Michael Woodbridge, London-based cybersecurity partner at Grant Thornton. US CONCERNS AIM AT AGENTIC AI The US regulatory inquiries centre on how banks use agentic AI in areas such as cybersecurity, focusing on whether AI agents are being used to identify, prioritize and respond to threats. Questions from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Fed focus on what limits are placed on systems, how their actions are monitored and approved and whether banks can clearly track and audit AI agent decisions, two of the people said. They are also asking what safeguards exist to prevent agents from exceeding their authority, whether humans remain involved in key decisions and how banks can shut down autonomous systems. The OCC, the Fed and the FDIC declined to comment. Through their questions, regulators are probing more specific issues tied to advanced AI models, including the use of autonomous AI agents, foreign-developed models and new cyber risks, the three people with knowledge of their thinking said. The written and verbal inquiries to large, mid-size and smaller banks show regulators are focusing on vulnerabilities from banks' use of AI and their preparedness to act, they added. Regulators are still gathering information and are not yet being prescriptive about what lenders should be doing, they said. EUROPEANS WORRY ABOUT RECOVERY Supervisors in Britain are separately encouraging the largest banks to examine so-called bare metal recovery plans, two of the people familiar with their thinking said. These systems are entirely independent from a bank's main tech set-up and can kick in if primary operating systems are compromised. Building and maintaining such state-of-the-art recovery is expensive, however, the people said. Rather than introduce new requirements, UK authorities intend to work collaboratively with industry, they added. The BoE declined to comment. The ECB in July gave lenders an end-October deadline to [USN:L8N4390I3 TEXT:"produce plans to counter AI-enabled cyber threats"], including improved back-up and recovery. Asked about its strategy for regulating AI, the ECB referred to its July letter as well as a June speech by board member Frank Elderson who stressed the need to create a sense of urgency, not alarm, about the threats. The need for supervisory action has taken on added urgency after European banks and regulators [USN:L6N4130SI TEXT:"expressed frustration"] at getting limited access to Mythos this year, amid concerns US banks will be given first sight to test frontier models. Like their US counterparts, UK supervisors are also asking banks to use frontier AI to identify vulnerabilities and accelerate patching, two people said, with one adding that lenders were so far doing a good job. The third person said euro zone banks were also being asked to map how AI is being used across their businesses and third-party providers, to understand key dependencies and ensure they can switch off and restart systems in a controlled manner. Significant gaps remained at some firms, they added. "To protect against attacks, rapid recovery matters as much as prevention," said Sukand Ramachandran, managing director and senior partner at BCG. Without separately held clean, secure copies of critical data, "a serious attack could lock customers out of their accounts and disrupt payments across the wider economy", Ramachandran told Reuters.

item.title: 仏ＬＶＭＨ、第3四半期売上高は予想下回る 中国市場悪化が打撃
item.description:
Tassilo Hummel Alessandro Parodi
[パリ １２日 ロイター] - フランスの高級ブラン...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
仏ＬＶＭＨ、第3四半期売上高は予想下回る　中国市場悪化が打撃 10/13 14:00 配信

LVMHのロゴ。4月23日、パリで撮影。REUTERS/Stephanie Lecocq

Tassilo Hummel　Alessandro Parodi

[パリ １２日 ロイター] - フランスの高級ブランド大手、モエ・ヘネシー・ルイ・ヴィトン（ＬＶＭＨ）が１２日発表した２０２６年第３・四半期決算は、為替変動の影響を除いたオーガニック売上高が前年同期比１％増の１８５億ユーロ（約２０７億ドル）となり、伸び率は調査会社ビジブル・アルファがまとめた市場予想の１．３％に届かなかった。

中国の消費者の購買意欲が急激に悪化し、主力ブランドのルイ・ヴィトンやクリスチャン・ディオールの販売に打撃を与えたのが要因。年間３５００億ドル規模の高級ブランド業界は３年連続で縮小しており、ＬＶＭＨの業績が予想を下回ったことは回復に苦戦するとの懸念を強めることになりそうだ。

バッグ「バーキン」で知られるフランスの高級ブランド大手エルメスと、グッチを抱えるケリングは第３・四半期決算を来週公表する。

欧州高級ブランド大手の時価総額は今年に入ってから約３３００億ユーロ減っており、ＬＶＭＨだけでも約４０％の喪失。決算発表後にＬＶＭＨの米国上場株は３％超下落した。

ＬＶＭＨの売上高の半分弱を占めるファッション・皮革製品部門のオーガニック売上高は前年同期比で５％減り、減少率は市場予想の１．８％より大きかった。

米銀行大手バンク・オブ・アメリカのアナリストらは顧客向けのメモで「決算内容は、業界全体にとって引き続きマイナス要因となる可能性が高いと考えている」と指摘した。

ＲＢＣのアナリスト、ピラル・ダダニア氏は、決算発表を受けてＬＶＭＨや同業他社の株価に「軽微な圧力」がかかると予想していると言及した。

投資家の懸念をさらに強めているのは、ブルガリやティファニーなどのブランドを擁するＬＶＭＨの時計・宝飾品部門の成長率が６％と、２６年上半期の９％から鈍化したことだ。

多くの消費者がハンドバッグやファッションよりも価値が高いと見なしている「ハード・ラグジュアリー」部門は、これまで景気後退の影響をおおむね免れてきた。しかし、一部のアナリストは最近、ハード・ラグジュアリーの回復力が弱まりつつある可能性があると警告している。

中国がけん引するアジア地域の第３・四半期の売上高は前年同期比で５％減。一方、米国では５％伸びた。

ＬＶＭＨのセシル・カバニス最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）はアナリストらに対して「特に第３・四半期は、アジアはマクロ経済要因による中国の消費者心理の急激な悪化の影響を受け、自由裁量支出に顕著な影響が及んだ」と説明した。

中国は世界の高級品購入額の約５分の１を占めており、長らく成長を引っ張ってきた。しかし、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック（世界的大流行）後に需要が急激に弱まっている。

ＬＶＭＨのファッション・皮革製品部門は、グループ内で群を抜いて大きいルイ・ヴィトンが主導している。だが、最近は勢いが鈍っている。

ルイ・ヴィトンは、中国の飲料店チェーン「モリーティー」のロゴが、ルイ・ヴィトンのハンドバッグなどにあしらわれている「モノグラム・フラワー」と呼ばれる花の模様に酷似しているとして商標権侵害で提訴した。ただ、この訴訟に対しては中国国内で反発する声が出ている。

クリスチャン・ディオールのように、ルイ・ヴィトンもクリエイティブ・ディレクターを交代させる可能性があるのかどうかを問われたカバニス氏は、コメントを差し控えた。その上で、ルイ・ヴィトンは革新と伝統の適切なバランスを見いだす必要があるとし、ブランドの再生には値下げのような「抜本的な措置」を講じるべきではないとの見解を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：フランスの大規模学生デモ、公教育の機能低下が背景　富裕層は私立へ コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 コラム：円急伸で揺らぐキャリートレード、見つからない次の調達通貨 焦点：仏、財政赤字巡り政局緊迫　大統領選控え市場の不安と格下げ警戒 アングル：スウィフトさんのドレス公開待つ婚礼業界、新トレンド取り込みへ準備着々 最終更新: 10/13(火) 14:00 ロイター

item.title: ＡＩブームが世界貿易押し上げ、中印などアジアに恩恵＝ＩＭＦ
item.description: [バンコク １３日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のチーフエコノミスト、シルバナ・テンレイロ氏は１３日、人工知...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＡＩブームが世界貿易押し上げ、中印などアジアに恩恵＝ＩＭＦ 10/13 13:59 配信

国際通貨基金（IMF）のチーフエコノミスト、シルバナ・テンレイロ氏ら。10月13日、タイのバンコクで撮影。REUTERS/Patipat Janthong

[バンコク １３日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のチーフエコノミスト、シルバナ・テンレイロ氏は１３日、人工知能（ＡＩ）に対する旺盛な需要が中国やインドなどアジア諸国の成長を押し上げているとし、ＡＩ関連貿易の伸びは世界貿易全体を上回っていると述べた。

バンコクで開かれているＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会で記者団に対し、ＡＩによる押し上げがなければ、世界貿易の伸びははるかに低い水準にとどまっていただろうと指摘した。

ＡＩ関連の投資・貿易の活況は世界成長の主要な原動力となっているが、ＡＩのサプライチェーン（供給網）は少数の国・分野に集中しており、供給の制約につながる恐れがあると述べた。

同氏によると、世界貿易が２０２３─２５年に８．３％拡大したのに対し、ＡＩ関連の世界貿易は２９％増加した。ＡＩ関連の貿易がなければ、全体の貿易の伸びは４．６％にとどまっていたという。

ＩＭＦは、市場価値の調整やサイバーセキュリティーに対するＡＩの脅威が成長の重しとなり、金融安定リスクを高める可能性があるとも警告した。テンレイロ氏によると、ＩＭＦの基本シナリオではＡＩブームが時間の経過とともに沈静化すると想定しているが、別のシナリオでは、ＡＩブームの長期化が実際に生産性向上につながった場合、インフレへの影響を抑えられる可能性が示されたという。

同氏は、ＡＩブームが続いても生産性向上につながらなければ、成長への押し上げ効果は小さくなり、インフレ率は高まると指摘。また、ＡＩによる収益性向上の評価が見直されれば、需要が下方修正されることになるとし、「基本的に、今われわれが目にしているブームが巻き戻されるということだ」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ＡＩ相場に迫る試練、過剰な期待示す不穏な兆候 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か 最終更新: 10/13(火) 13:59 ロイター

South Korea says US raises intelligence cooperation concerns, Yonhap says

SEOUL: South Korea's ambassador to the United States said Washington had raised concerns about intelligence cooperation between the allies and that Seoul had not yet fully addressed US expectations, Yonhap news agency reported on Tuesday (Oct 13). Ambassador Kang Kyung-wha told a South Korean parliamentary audit in Washington that intelligence sharing was the most difficult issue in bilateral relations, according to Yonhap. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio raised the matter during talks with South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun last month, Kang said. Kang did not detail Washington's concerns, but said communication between the two countries' intelligence agencies was continuing and had made progress.

The ambassador also said access to senior White House officials had been limited, according to the report. South Korea's foreign ministry did not immediately have a response to a Reuters request for comment on the report. South Korean media have reported that Washington asked that Seoul's National Intelligence Service be excluded from a June meeting with US and Japanese officials on North Korean cyber threats. Seoul's spy agency said the matter reflected a past misunderstanding and had been resolved, acknowledging restrictions on some intelligence connected to the earlier dispute but denying reports that the US had reduced sharing of North Korean missile information or cut the overall flow of intelligence. Kang said Seoul and Washington were discussing ways to secure South Korean rights to enrich uranium and reprocess spent nuclear fuel, either through revising their civil nuclear agreement or an additional arrangement. No progress had been made towards a summit between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, despite Trump signalling openness to dialogue, Kang said. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung told a cabinet meeting on Tuesday that Seoul should avoid subservient attitudes in dealings with other countries. Lee called the US alliance a central pillar of South Korean diplomacy which should be further developed, while adding that differences between countries were inevitable and should be managed through discussion and coordination.

item.title: AI investment props up global growth, but war and debt threaten outlook, IMF says
item.description: The IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1 per cent, a slight uptick from the 3.0 per cent it predicted in July.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

AI investment props up global growth, but war and debt threaten outlook, IMF says

The IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1 per cent, a slight uptick from the 3.0 per cent it predicted in July.

The logo of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings at Queen Sirikit National Convention Center in Bangkok, Thailand, on Oct 9, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Athit Perawongmetha)

FAST

BANGKOK: The global economy will still manage to top 3 per cent real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday. Despite a more protracted conflict that has kept oil prices above US$100 a barrel , the IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1 per cent, a slight uptick from the 3.0 per cent it predicted in July. The World Economic Outlook forecast, released as global economic and finance leaders gather in Bangkok for the IMF and World Bank annual meetings, is about even with the most optimistic scenario issued in April but below 2025 global growth of 3.5 per cent. For 2027, the IMF predicts 3.4 per cent global growth, flat with the July forecast and up 0.2 percentage points from April.

The slight improvement is largely due to continued strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure, prompting growth upgrades for key advanced economies building AI platforms and especially for countries supplying AI hardware, including South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico and Thailand, which is hosting the meetings this week. "The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits, so we need to move from just coping to rebuilding," the IMF's chief economist, Silvana Tenreyro, told a news conference. "We need to restore fiscal space. We need to rebuild supply-side resilience." She said major downside risks to growth include a prolonged, intensified war in the Middle East that spikes inflation pressures, rising bond yields that raise government borrowing costs, El Nino-driven extreme weather events and a reassessment of AI profitability that craters investment and asset prices. Countries and companies moved quickly to mitigate the oil price shock, drawing down reserves, substituting other suppliers and energy sources and cutting oil demand, Petya Koeva Brooks, the IMF's deputy research director, told Reuters in a separate interview. She said global growth would have fallen to 2.5 per cent this year without these measures, but their effect is fading as the war drags on. The IMF noted a growing divergence between countries benefiting from AI and those bypassed by it. Just 32 countries now account for 95 per cent of global growth, compared to 54 countries in April. Downward growth revisions have become more widespread, with the IMF downgrading 47 per cent of economies since the April forecasts were issued, including several energy importers outside AI value chains. Hardest hit by downgrades were the Gulf countries directly impacted by the US-Israeli war against Iran , with Saudi Arabia's GDP now forecast to contract 3.3 per cent this year compared with the 1.7 per cent growth predicted in July. Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are also expected to fall into deep recessions, with 2026 contractions of 7.6 per cent, 16 per cent, 16.7 per cent, 15.6 per cent and 3.9 per cent, respectively.

Related:

WTO lifts global trade outlook as AI boom powers Asian growth

WTO warns of 'most serious and sustained' trade disruptions

UNITED STATES FLAT, IMPROVEMENT IN EUROPE Among major economies, the IMF forecast US growth of 2.3 per cent for both 2026 and 2027, unchanged for this year and 0.1 percentage point higher for next year. The US economy is expected to be supported by robust private consumption, tax cuts and AI investment, though the boost from AI will be offset by its large import content. Eurozone growth for 2026 was upgraded to 1.1 per cent from 0.9 per cent in July due to stronger investment in AI, participation in AI value chains such as chemical production in Germany, and higher defence spending in EU countries. Britain's 2026 growth forecast also was upgraded by 0.3 percentage points from July to 1.3 per cent due to larger AI investment. The IMF forecast China's growth at 4.5 per cent for 2026 and 4.0 per cent for 2027, both down 0.1 percentage point from July, as higher oil prices exacerbate weak domestic demand despite strong exports. India remains the world's fastest-growing major economy at 7.0 per cent for both 2026 and 2027, up 0.6 percentage point this year and 0.3 percentage point next year compared with the July forecasts amid robust domestic demand, services activity and AI investment. The AI investment surge is projected to keep upward pressure on prices, with global headline consumer price inflation forecast at 4.7 per cent in 2026 and 4.1 per cent for 2027.

Related:

AI productivity gains may not curb inflation, IMF's Tenreyro warns

AI is creating an economy that can grow without needing more workers. Should we be worried?

ENERGY PRICE, AI RISKS Participants at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok will be assessing a precarious outlook. The IMF forecasts are based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen in March 2027 with a broad return to pre-war shipping conditions occurring by October 2027. The IMF assumes an average oil price of US$96 per barrel for 2026 and US$87 in 2027. But under an adverse scenario highlighted in the report, in which a worsening war pushes oil prices to US$130 per barrel through the first quarter of 2027, growth would be reduced by 0.2 percentage point in 2026 and 0.5 percentage point in 2027. Inflation in 2027 would surge by another 1.1 percentage point to 5.2 per cent. AI is also a huge source of uncertainty, with major downside and upside risks, the IMF report said. Under a scenario of faster adoption of the technology and accelerated investment, global GDP could rise a further 0.6 per cent by 2029, with the bulk of the benefits going to the US and China. But if productivity gains from AI fail to materialise, prompting a sharp decline in investment, US GDP could fall by 0.8 per cent directly, causing spillovers to Asian technology exporters with a total direct GDP impact of as much as 0.4 per cent by 2028. This shift would also trigger a sharp reduction in asset prices and tighter financial conditions that cause a major drop in consumption, particularly in the US, the IMF said. Higher global bond yields would further reduce activity, with a combined global output reduction of 1.1 per cent by 2028, including a 1.8 per cent drop in US output. The IMF also warned that elevated public debt levels, particularly in advanced economies, increase the risk of sharply higher borrowing costs that can weigh on growth prospects. It urged governments to stop delaying action to rebuild fiscal buffers and articulate credible medium-term plans to bring debt back to sustainable levels - advice that IMF officials plan to push at the Bangkok meetings.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: Gold holds steady ahead of US inflation data, Warsh remarks
item.description: Gold prices were largely steady on Tuesday, as investors looked out for key US inflation data and remarks from the Federal Reserve Chair later this week to gauge future monetary policy.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Gold prices were largely steady on Tuesday, as investors looked out for key US inflation data and remarks from the Federal Reserve Chair later this week to gauge future monetary policy. Spot gold fell 0.1% to $4,164.70 per ounce by 11:26 a.m. EDT (1526 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery were down 0.1% at $4,188.40 per ounce. "We have some inflation data that's coming out later this week. So market is kind of waiting to see how that plays out," said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX. He noted the Fed chairman will deliver his last speech before the upcoming rate meeting on Thursday, and anticipates a quieter session ahead of Wednesday's and Thursday's events. Investors are looking ahead to the Consumer Price Index data on Wednesday, while Thursday's Producer Price Index figures and remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will be closely parsed. Fed Governor Christopher Waller on Tuesday said the recent rise in US bond yields reflects stronger economic growth rather than higher [USN:L1N45Z0AY TEXT:"inflation expectations"], which remain "well anchored." Gold loses its appeal in a high-interest-rate environment as it does not yield interest. Currently, traders see only a 19% chance of a Fed rate hike this month but are pricing in an 88% chance of a December increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool . Meanwhile, oil prices fell on Tuesday and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week. The dollar and benchmark 10-year Treasury yields slipped from their respective highs, but still hovered near elevated levels. The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday highlighted risks from elevated public debt levels and [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"rising bond yields"] that may be driven higher still by war-driven inflation pressures. "Interest rate hikes have increasingly become a double-edged sword for gold. While higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as gold, they also intensify the fiscal burden on many governments and thereby exacerbate debt sustainability concerns," analysts at Commerzbank said in a note. Elsewhere, spot silver fell 1.5% to $59.44 per ounce, platinum edged 0.8% lower to $1,672.25 per ounce and palladium dropped 1.3% to $1,128.45 per ounce.

FAST

NEW YORK: The International Monetary Fund trimmed its growth forecasts for Latin America and the Caribbean for this year and next and said most of the region was getting little lift from the artificial intelligence boom that has helped other economies absorb the energy shock from the Middle East war. In its World Economic Outlook, released early on Tuesday (Oct 13) in Bangkok, the Fund projected regional growth of 2.3 per cent this year. That is down from 2.5 per cent growth in 2025 and from its July forecast of 2.4 per cent growth for 2026. The IMF cut its 2027 forecast to 2.5 per cent from 2.7 per cent. The regional downgrades come even as the Fund nudged up its world growth forecast for this year to 3.1 per cent from July's 3.0 per cent, crediting rerouted energy supplies and AI-driven investment for the resilience of what it calls a split global economy. The Middle East war has turned energy into a global inflation shock, with Brent crude about 45 per cent above its prewar level. Higher fuel and power costs are squeezing households and businesses, while fears of persistent inflation have helped push global borrowing costs to multidecade highs.

In Latin America, the IMF said, the energy shock's effect depends on whether gains for commodity exporters outweigh losses for energy importers and on how credible central banks' inflation targets are, adding that "there is little offset from the technology upturn in most countries." Of the three Latin American economies the IMF listed separately in its July World Economic Outlook update, Argentina took the deepest cut in its output estimate. The Fund now expects Argentine growth to slow to 2.1 per cent this year from 4.5 per cent in 2025, well below the 3.5 per cent it forecast in July, and it lowered its 2027 forecast to 3.5 per cent from 4.0 per cent. The report shows inflation is forecast to fall to 32.5 per cent this year from 41.9 per cent in 2025. Brazil's forecasts fell to 2.2 per cent for this year and 1.9 per cent for 2027, from 2.4 per cent and 2.2 per cent in July, when the IMF had expected Brazilian growth to "remain resilient" this year. The Fund now expects growth to slow next year, citing still-restrictive monetary conditions aimed at bringing inflation back to target, the withdrawal of government fiscal support and global uncertainty. Mexico moved the other way, with its 2026 forecast raised to 1.5 per cent from 1.2 per cent. The Fund previously linked Mexico's expected pickup to less restrictive domestic policies. It now points to exports, including through AI supply chains, and to investment that is stabilising as growth quickens next year. Even so, it trimmed Mexico's 2027 forecast to 1.8 per cent from 1.9 per cent and said trade and other uncertainties would keep holding back activity. The report's tables show Chile's growth slowing to 0.6 per cent this year from 2.5 per cent, Bolivia's economy shrinking 3.0 per cent after a 1.6 per cent contraction in 2025, and Venezuelan inflation speeding up to 467.9 per cent from 252.0 per cent. The IMF said risks remain tilted to the downside. It warned that market turmoil could hit emerging economies through higher government borrowing costs, pressure on their currencies and tighter local financial conditions.

item.title: Dollar slips from 18-month high as oil prices fall, inflation data in focus
item.description: The dollar slipped from an 18-month high on Tuesday as oil prices retreated and investors reassessed the AI-fueled rally that has supported demand for US assets this year, while awaiting fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate path.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo, Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: The dollar slipped from an 18-month high on Tuesday as oil prices retreated and investors reassessed the AI-fueled rally that has supported demand for US assets this year, while awaiting fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate path. Markets expect US President Donald Trump to avoid escalation in the Middle East , as a wider conflict could hurt his standing ahead of the midterm elections next month. Trump said last week the [USN:L1N45U0PH TEXT:"US will not attack Iran"] before the elections, and [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"mentioned an energy ceasefire"] between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday. [USN:L1N45Z00X TEXT:"Oil prices fell"] 0.86% to $105.75 per barrel on Tuesday, as traders weighed the prospect of additional Russian diesel supplies. Russia said it can restore diesel exports [USN:S8N45E0D7 TEXT:"beyond levels"] Trump outlined in a deal with Moscow. "The dollar (is) a little weaker on slightly lower oil. Large bank earnings this morning were mixed, shedding little light on the broader equity outlook," said John Velis, Americas macro strategist at BNY. "With bond yields slightly off recent highs, the dollar looks to trade slightly softer on the day." Beyond energy , some analysts said the dollar's recent rally is also being challenged by growing doubts about the artificial intelligence-driven investment story. "In our view, the 'US exceptionalism' trade has once again become overextended, and is exposed to a technical pullback," said Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay in Toronto. The US dollar index , a measure of the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, slid 0.25% to 102.27 after reaching 102.61 on Monday, its highest level since April 2025. Investors are now awaiting the release on Wednesday of the US Consumer Price Index for September, which should provide further clues about possible Fed policy tightening. Traders see about an 80% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 51% a month ago, while pricing in about 75 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. "This report will have to factor in this escalation we have seen particularly on the Saudi front. I wouldn't be surprised if the numbers are worse than expected," said Erik Bregar, director of FX and precious metals risk management at Silver Gold Bull in Toronto. "I'd go with a December rate-hike odds. I think the market is rationally priced for one more hike." Investors abandoned bets on a Fed rate hike later this month after two policymakers argued for gathering [USN:L6N45N16X TEXT:"more evidence before deciding"] whether further tightening is needed, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller said [USN:L1N45Z0AY TEXT:"inflation expectations remained "well anchored.""] Rising oil prices recently have been supporting the dollar at the expense of currencies such as the euro and yen, which are linked to economies far more dependent than the US on imported oil. EURO REBOUNDS DESPITE GAS PRICES HITTING HIGHS The euro rebounded from a roughly 17-month low on Tuesday despite another jump in gas prices, a key driver of euro zone inflation, while concerns over France's fiscal outlook persisted. It was up 0.3% at $1.1189 after hitting $1.11525 on Monday, its lowest level since May 2025. The slower pace of ECB rate hikes "would likely cause further euro/dollar downside," said Thierry Wizman, global forex and rates strategist at Macquarie Group. Natural gas prices in Europe rose to their highest level since December 2022 and were last at €86.71 per megawatt-hour. The yen strengthened 0.15% to 158.38 against the dollar after Bank of Japan data showed [USN:L4N45Y1EW TEXT:"wholesale prices"] rose 6.8% in the year to September, missing a median market forecast of 7.6% but still enough to justify market fears of higher interest rates. Investors continued to see support from the prospect of further BoJ policy tightening, and the risk of official intervention against excessive currency moves. The euro was last up 0.21% at 177.32 versus the Japanese currency , after hitting 176.25, its lowest level since November 2025. The Australian dollar was at $0.6979, following the release of the [USN:P8N44M01S TEXT:"minutes"] from the Reserve Bank of Australia's September board meeting. The board voted unanimously to raise rates for the fourth time this year.

item.title: RJ Mitte, Breaking Bad actor and disability rights advocate, dies at 34
item.description: RJ Mitte rose to fame playing Walter White Jr in the acclaimed television series Breaking Bad. He drew on his personal experience with cerebral palsy to portray the character.
item.dc:creator: CNA Lifestyle
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Entertainment

RJ Mitte, Breaking Bad actor and disability rights advocate, dies at 34

RJ Mitte rose to fame playing Walter White Jr in the acclaimed television series Breaking Bad. He drew on his personal experience with cerebral palsy to portray the character.

Actor RJ Mitte poses at the premiere for 'El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie' in Los Angeles, California, U.S., October 7, 2019. REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni/File Photo

FAST

Actor RJ Mitte, whose personal experience living with cerebral palsy informed his role as Walter White Jr, the physically disabled son of a methamphetamine kingpin in the landmark television show Breaking Bad, died on Monday (Oct 12) at age 34. News of Mitte's death in Brownsville, Texas, was confirmed in a statement released through the talent management agency that represented the actor. No other details about the circumstances of his death were given. "It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," the statement said. Drawing from his real-life experience with cerebral palsy, Mitte was best known for his breakout role on the AMC cable TV series Breaking Bad, playing the only son of the lead character, Walter White, a terminally ill high school teacher who descends into a secret life of crime cooking crystal meth. Mitte's character, who adopted the nickname Flynn, used crutches and spoke with a slur, gains greater prominence as the story arc of the series progressed. He starts out as a carefree teenager who largely admires his father but later struggles to reckon with the family' disintegration as the truth about Walter White's "Heisenberg" alter ego emerges. "Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement said, noting that the actor was active in a number of philanthropic organizations devoted to fundraising and awareness for cerebral palsy and other muscle-control disorders. The acclaimed series, often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time, ran from 2008-2013, garnering 16 Emmy awards, including two for best drama series. He later played a high school wrestler with cerebral palsy in the 2021 coming-of-age drama Triumph. He was a Screen Actors Guild spokesman for performers with disabilities, and a celebrity ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy.

Source: Reuters/mm

item.title: Saudi warning system stayed silent before deadly airport attacks
item.description: The government has not said why there were no alerts to the public. Their absence raises questions about Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to attack and about its ability to protect residents and visitors.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings of imminent military attacks days before a series of deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300. The government has not said why there were no alerts to the public before the four [USN:L6N45Y0OR TEXT:"Riyadh attacks"] in the past week. The warnings had served to highlight the violence undermining the kingdom's efforts to project an image of calm to its people and the world during its war with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis. Their absence during the [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"airport strikes"] raised questions about Saudi Arabia's vulnerability to attack and about its ability to protect residents and visitors, four Western and Arab officials in the region and political analysts told Reuters. It also reflected efforts to maintain a sense of normalcy, they said. "They (the Saudi government) want to have it both ways: to launch a military operation and at the same time try to give confidence to the population and external stakeholders," said Sultan Alamer, a US-based Saudi academic and Senior Resident Fellow at the Middle East Policy Council think tank. The Saudi civil defence - a national emergency management, rescue and firefighting agency which operates under the interior ministry and issues early warning alerts - and the Saudi government media office did not respond to emailed questions on why no alerts were issued. Saudi Arabia's approach is also one that some regional analysts said risked backfiring because the absence of warnings has heightened uncertainty in the kingdom. On Monday, Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority issued its first alerts since September 29, warning of potential threats in Riyadh and southern cities. Reuters was unable to ascertain whether the decision to issue alerts again was a response to the airport attacks, and the Saudi government did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter. SYSTEM GOES SILENT All Gulf countries have been hit by Iranian drones and missiles since the US-Iran war began in February, but their governments have handled public warnings differently. Qatar's interior ministry has issued mobile phone alerts before nearly every attack, including most recent attacks in July, when residents were warned to stay inside and away from windows. Bahrain and Kuwait have repeatedly sounded sirens urging people to take shelter. Saudi Arabia began issuing threat alerts to mobile phones and social media accounts via a national early warning system in May. But despite increasing Houthi attacks leading up to last week, the system went silent. The last alert before last week's attacks was issued on September 29, for the southern province of Najran, according to posts on the civil defence X account. The civil defences authority has continued to issue warnings about staying out of harm's way during adverse weather, including rain and flooding, and did so as recently as Monday. It also warned residents not to share images, rumours or information about interceptions and impact sites, including in a post on Monday, under government regulations issued in March. Reuters could not determine whether anyone had faced prosecution for sharing such information, and the Saudi government media office did not respond to a request for comment on the matter. Before last week's airport attacks, officials from an allied Western government asked Saudi authorities why the alerts had stopped, two officials with direct knowledge of the matter said. The response was that the alerts were too disruptive and many citizens had complained they were being woken by them at night, the officials said. The Saudi government media office and Saudi officials did not respond to requests for comment on the assertion. Former US ambassador to Saudi Arabia Michael Ratney said Riyadh was trying to balance public messaging on attacks with efforts to prevent disruption in the kingdom but had ended up adding to a sense of unease about the strikes. "Their approach to public messaging seems like a corollary to the quandary they are in: They need to respond to the Houthis but don't want that to result in societal disruption and their public messaging is a reflection of that," he said. "But the lack of alerts of incoming Houthi attacks creates the very nervousness they are trying to avoid." NEW THREAT ALERT Ali Shihabi, a Saudi analyst close to the government, said that with or without early warnings, the kingdom would struggle to defend all of its assets because of its size. "In Saudi Arabia you have too much to protect. It's a huge country with airports, pipelines and oil facilities. There is just not enough coverage to defend everything at once, not enough Patriots (missile defence systems), interceptors and missile batteries to do it all," he said. "Saudi Arabia has an unlimited need for air defences," he added." Despite the attacks, Saudi Arabia hosted an international conference on Monday, though major [USN:L6N45Y0GT TEXT:"oil bosses"] dropped out. At the World Petroleum Council Energy Congress in Riyadh, Saudi Prince Abdulaziz bin Salaman, a brother of the Saudi crown prince and the kingdom's energy minister, struck a defiant tone while acknowledging risks and Saudi Arabia's intent to keep its economic plans on track.He thanked all who had travelled to Riyadh "because you know this country is safe" but added: "Our gathering here does not mean the risk is gone.""We will never forfeit any chance to maintain our commitment and our vision," he said. EMBASSIES ISSUE THEIR OWN INTERNAL ALERTS Despite no public alerts being issued this month until Monday, Riyadh has been attacked about a dozen times, two of the Western officials said. During that time, Western embassies in the kingdom have been issuing their own internal missile and drone alerts to staff, according to three people familiar with the matter and alerts seen by Reuters. These internal alerts are compiled from a mixture of US and other Western government intelligence and input from Saudi authorities, one of those people said. They include alerts sent to staff around the time of two first airport strikes last week according to the people familiar with the matter. They said that even the embassies had received no internal warning before Saturday's airport strike, without offering an explanation. Reuters could not determine why no warning came before Saturday's attack, the deadliest of last week's attacks. On Sunday, Saudi state TV released footage of Saturday's strike. It showed several shots of travellers in the airport terminal. Dozens lined up to board a flight. Men and women sat in chairs waiting, their eyes trained on the screens of their mobile phones as they scrolled. Then, the bright orange flash of a missile explosion.

item.title: First major Irish public sector strike in almost two decades set to go ahead
item.description: Much of Ireland's public sector is set to go on strike for the first time since the height of the country's financial crisis in 2009, after trade unions rejected a late bid by the government to avert the stoppage.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Much of Ireland's public sector is set to go on strike for the first time since the height of the country's financial crisis in 2009, after trade unions rejected a late bid by the government to avert the stoppage. Some 300,000 teachers, health workers, civil servants and other public workers plan to hold the one-day strike over a deadlock between unions and the government on the basis for entering talks on public sector pay rises. Unions have for months argued that pay terms must be agreed before other issues, such as productivity, were discussed due to cost-of-living pressures. Ministers have rejected this condition and say it represents a break from previous deals. In a letter to union leaders on Monday urging them to postpone the strike action, Public Expenditure Minister Jack Chambers said "pay issues can and should be discussed as a priority alongside other matters". The chair of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions public services committee said union leaders could not see how this represented any change in Chambers' position or provided a basis for postponement. A series of pay increases have kept industrial peace since the harsh pay cuts that spurred the 2009 walkout, and while Ireland's economy and public finances are among the healthiest in Europe, high prices have frustrated many workers. Trade unions want any new deal to cover the gap between pay and inflation over previous years and ensure that wages will not fall behind living standards over the duration of any new deal. The last pay deal expired at the end of June. Essential services such as emergency hospital departments will be maintained on Wednesday and public transport will also be unaffected. However fire and ambulance services will run a reduced service and hospitals have warned of "significant and widespread" disruption with routine procedures cancelled. A second strike day is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21.

item.title: Airlines cancel flights to Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attacks
item.description: Airlines are cancelling flights to Saudi Arabia following the deadly weekend attacks on Riyadh airport by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, extending disruption to air travel across the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airlines are cancelling flights to Saudi Arabia following the [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"deadly weekend attacks"] on Riyadh airport by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, extending disruption to air travel across the region. The airport will be closed until October 17, according to a Notice to Airmen issued on Monday. Here's a list of airlines that have taken measures, in alphabetical order: AIR FRANCE-KLM (AIRF.PA) The Franco-Dutch group has extended a previous suspension of services to and from the Saudi capital until the end of October. AIR INDIA The Indian carrier has extended the suspension of flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 17. AKASA AIR (SNVA.NS) The Mumbai-based budget carrier has suspended flights to and from Jeddah and Riyadh until October 17. CATHAY PACIFIC (0293.HK) The Hong Kong flag carrier postponed the resumption of its Hong Kong–Dubai and Hong Kong–Riyadh routes through January 31, 2027. DELTA (DAL.N) The American airline said it would delay its planned flights from Atlanta to Riyadh until March 2027. ETIHAD AIRWAYS The Abu Dhabi-based carrier cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, as well as 10 flights to Dammam and Jeddah, until October 19. GULF AIR Bahrain's flag carrier cancelled its flights to and from Riyadh from October 12 to October 17. INDIGO Flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah remain cancelled until October 17. LUFTHANSA (LHAG.DE) Carriers owned by the German airline group have cancelled all flights to Riyadh until October 16. MALAYSIA AIRLINES The Kuala Lumpur-based flag carrier cancelled flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah until October 17 as a precautionary measure. PHILIPPINE AIRLINES The national flag carrier of the Philippines extended the suspension of its flights to and from Riyadh until November 29. QATAR AIRWAYS The Qatari carrier has temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam.

item.content:encoded:

The notion that stocks and bonds follow a rational path has been widely debunked. But are idiosyncrasies becoming more visible? item.description: Reporter Jeff Horwitz reflects on his Hollywood alter ego, and the reporting that landed on the big screen.
item.content:encoded:
Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app.

Reporter Jeff Horwitz is having a surreal week. His investigation into Facebook has been turned into a major Hollywood film starring Jeremy Allen White. On this episode of On Assignment , the Pulitzer Prize-winning Reuters journalist reflects on the Facebook Files investigation, his relationship with whistleblower Frances Haugen, and the impact the revelations had on the debate over social media's harms. He also shares what it's like to see his own story transformed for the big screen in Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning . item.title: Inside China's AI race
item.description: What does the fight to dominate AI look like from inside China?
item.content:encoded:
Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app.

As the US and China race to dominate artificial intelligence, Reuters correspondents Eduardo Baptista and Laurie Chen say the two countries aren't even playing the same game. On this episode of On Assignment, they take us inside China's AI industry - from Beijing's push to weave AI into every corner of society, to the murky world of chip access, distillation and export controls. Hear what it takes to report on one of the most fast-moving industries on Earth, and why the answer to "who's winning" may depend entirely on how you define the race. item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: Wall Street ouvre dans le désordre après les résultats des banques
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ouvre dans le désordre après les résultats des banques PARIS, 13 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a ouvert en ordre dispersé mardi alors que les investisseurs analysent les premiers résultats trimestriels des entreprises avec le coup d'envoi donné par les grandes banques américaines. LVMH: Les ventes au T3 ravivent les doutes sur la reprise du secteur du luxe 13 octobre (Reuters) - Les ventes de la division Mode et Maroquinerie de LVMH, inférieures aux attentes au troisième trimestre en raison d'un affaiblissement de la demande des consommateurs chinois pour sa marque phare, Louis Vuitton, ravivent les interrogations sur les perspectives de reprise du secteur du luxe. Boeing a livré 57 avions en septembre, son meilleur mois depuis le début de l'année SEATTLE, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Boeing a annoncé mardi avoir livré 57 avions en septembre, après 51 en août et 55 un an plus tôt, marquant son meilleur résultat mensuel depuis le début de l'année. Citi: Bénéfice au-dessus des attentes au T3 avec la banque d'investissement, les services et la gestion de patrimoine 13 octobre (Reuters) - Citigroup a dépassé mardi les attentes de Wall Street concernant son bénéfice du troisième trimestre, porté par la hausse des revenus issus de la banque d'investissement, des transactions avec des multinationales, ainsi qu'à l'augmentation des résultats de la gestion de patrimoine. JP Morgan: Hausse du bénéfice au T3, mais l'élan de la banque d'investissement faiblit 13 octobre (Reuters) - JP Morgan a fait état mardi d'une hausse du bénéfice au troisième trimestre, tandis que le ralentissement récent des opérations de fusion-acquisition suscite des inquiétudes. Le bénéfice de Goldman Sachs progresse au T3 grâce à la bonne tenue des actions 13 octobre (Reuters) - Goldman Sachs a fait état mardi d'une hausse de son bénéfice au troisième trimestre, porté par une activité de fusions-acquisitions stable et par la volatilité des marchés liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient, qui a stimulé les revenus liés aux actions. Wells Fargo: Hausse du bénéfice au T3 avec les revenus d'intérêts 13 octobre (Reuters) - Wells Fargo a publié mardi une hausse de son bénéfice au troisième trimestre, soutenue par la croissance de son portefeuille de prêts et l'augmentation de ses revenus d'intérêts. J&J: Bénéfice au T3 au-dessus des attentes mais le conflit au Moyen-Orient pèse sur les ventes 13 octobre (Reuters) - Johnson & Johnson a annoncé mardi un bénéfice trimestriel légèrement supérieur aux attentes, grâce aux ventes soutenues du Tremfya, un traitement contre les maladies immunitaires. Stellantis: Les États-Unis finiront bien par basculer vers les véhicules électriques, selon le DG PARIS, 13 octobre (Reuters) - L'électrification finira bien par s'imposer sur le marché automobile américain malgré une adoption jusqu'à présent lente des véhicules électriques, a déclaré mardi Antonio Filosa, directeur géneral de Stellantis. La GB doit poursuivre ses efforts de réduction du déficit, selon le FMI BANGKOK, 13 octobre (Reuters) - La Grande-Bretagne doit veiller à respecter ses plans de réduction du déficit alors que l'endettement public s'envole ailleurs, a averti mardi le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), alors que le ministre des Finances, John Healey, doit présenter son premier budget annuel à la fin du mois.

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: La coalition saoudienne ordonne d'évacuer un site pétrolier à Sanaa, les Houthis signalent une attaque
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La coalition saoudienne ordonne d'évacuer un site pétrolier à Sanaa, les Houthis signalent une attaque 13 octobre (Reuters) - La coalition armée dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite a appelé mardi la population civile à évacuer la zone de la station centrale d'Al-Sabah, une installation pétrolière située à Sanaa, la capitale yéménite, en vue d'une opération militaire. Le Hezbollah présente un plan d'aide aux Libanais déplacés 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le Hezbollah va verser une aide pouvant atteindre 14.000 dollars (12.500 euros) aux familles dont le domicile principal a été détruit ou rendu inhabitable au cours du conflit contre Israël cette année, a annoncé mardi le président du conseil exécutif du mouvement armé libanais. Un navire attaqué par un drone près de la Bulgarie, 11 marins disparus SOFIA, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Onze marins sont portés disparus mardi en mer Noire après le naufrage au large de la Bulgarie d'un navire touché par un drone. Le nombre de cas d'Ebola en RDC dépasse les 9.000, selon des données 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le nombre de cas confirmés d'Ebola en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) dépasse désormais les 9.000, selon des données gouvernementales publiées mardi. Pas de frappe russe sur des cibles énergétiques en Ukraine, une première depuis la "trêve" de Trump KYIV, 13 octobre (Reuters) - La Russie semble s'être abstenue de bombarder des infrastructures énergétiques en Ukraine pour la première fois depuis l'annonce dimanche par Donald Trump d'un "cessez-le-feu énergétique" entre les deux pays, selon le compte rendu quotidien des opérations nocturnes donné mardi par le ministère russe de la Défense. Le pape Léon XIV opéré d'un nodule pulmonaire mardi après-midi ROME, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV devait subir mardi après-midi une intervention chirurgicale, à l'hôpital Gemelli de Rome, pour le retrait d'un nodule pulmonaire détecté à un stade précoce, confirme le Vatican. Allemagne: Merz place la réforme de la protection sociale au-dessus de sa popularité FRANCFORT, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz a déclaré mardi être prêt à sacrifier sa popularité dans les sondages pour faire adopter des réformes du système de protection sociale qui, selon lui, auraient dû être mises en oeuvre il y a des années et profiteront aux jeunes. Andersson redit ne pas être en mesure de former un gouvernement STOCKHOLM, 13 octobre (Reuters) - La présidente du Parti social-démocrate suédois, Magdalena Andersson, a de nouveau annoncé mardi ne pas être en mesure d'obtenir un soutien suffisant pour former un nouveau gouvernement après la courte victoire du bloc de centre-gauche aux élections législatives du 13 septembre. Kyiv accuse Moscou d'avoir violé la "trêve énergétique" de Trump KYIV, 12 octobre (Reuters) - La Russie a frappé au moins six cibles énergétiques en Ukraine au cours d'une nuit et d'une matinée marquées par des bombardements meurtriers à travers le pays, a déclaré lundi le président Volodimir Zelensky, preuve selon lui que Moscou n'a aucun intérêt pour le cessez-le-feu annoncé par Donald Trump. La Corée du Nord expose un missile présenté comme capable d'atteindre les USA SEOUL, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Kim Jong-un a visité un musée de défense dans lequel est exposé un missile balistique intercontinental capable d'atteindre les Etats-Unis, a rapporté mardi l'agence de presse officielle KCNA, alors même que le président américain Donald Trump a de nouveau évoqué la possibilité de rencontrer le dirigeant nord-coréen.

item.title: OFRTP Summary
item.description: Le parquet antiterroriste se saisit de l'enquête sur les tirs au collège d'Aubagne
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le parquet antiterroriste se saisit de l'enquête sur les tirs au collège d'Aubagne PARIS, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le parquet national antiterroriste a annoncé mardi se saisir de l'enquête sur l'intrusion armée au collège Joseph-Lakanal d'Aubagne (Bouches-du-Rhône) d'un élève de l'établissement qui a ouvert le feu au fusil de chasse sur le proviseur et une enseignante, les blessant légèrement. La Russie condamne la saisie par la France d'un pétrolier au large de la Réunion MOSCOU, 13 octobre (Reuters) - L'ambassade de Russie à Paris a condamné mardi la saisie par la France du navire pétrolier DF Peak à 450 milles nautiques au large de la Réunion, annoncée la veille par Emmanuel Macron, la qualifiant d'acte de piraterie et de violation du droit international. Un élève ouvre le feu dans un collège d'Aubagne, le proviseur et une enseignante blessés Un élève de 14 ans a tiré au fusil de chasse lundi matin dans l'enceinte de son établissement, le collège Joseph-Lakanal d'Aubagne (Bouches-du-Rhône), blessant le principal et une enseignante, a confirmé le parquet de Marseille, qui a ouvert une enquête des chefs de "tentatives d'assassinat". Raphaël Glucksmann remporte la primaire social-démocrate dès le premier tour Le candidat Place Publique à l'élection présidentielle, Raphaël Glucksmann, a remporté dès le premier tour la primaire social-démocrate, a annoncé dimanche le Parti socialiste. La France appelle les autorités palestiniennes à revenir sur le report les élections La France regrette le report par le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas des élections législatives et présidentielle, a déclaré dimanche un porte-parole du ministère des Affaires étrangères, appelant les autorités palestiniennes à revenir sur cette décision. Nobel/Littérature: Le prix décerné à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. Les deux Renoir dérobés au musée de Cagnes-sur-Mer retrouvés Les deux tableaux dérobés il y a un peu plus d'un mois au musée Renoir de Cagnes-sur-Mer (Alpes-Maritimes) ont été retrouvés par la police et six suspects ont été arrêtés, a déclaré vendredi le maire Rassemblement national (RN) de la ville, Bryan Masson. L'Allemagne abandonne le projet de char commun avec la France-Mandon L'Allemagne a décidé d'abandonner le projet avec la France de char commun du futur, le MGCS ("Main Ground Combat System", système principal de combat terrestre), a annoncé jeudi le chef d'état-major des armées, Fabien Mandon, lors d'une audition devant une commission parlementaire. France-Dix millions de barils de gazole libérés des réserves pour baisser les prix à la pompe-Lecornu La France va libérer 10 millions de barils de gazole de ses réserves stratégiques avec l'objectif d'agir sur les prix à la pompe, qui devraient ainsi "mécaniquement baisser" de 12 centimes à 18 centimes d'euro par litre de gazole, a déclaré mercredi soir le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu. Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'actes de sabotage contre ses entreprises du secteur de la défense La Russie a lancé des opérations de sabotage contre des entreprises danoises fournissant l'Ukraine après avoir conclu que ses tentatives de perturbation à plus grande échelle n'avaient pas freiné le soutien militaire occidental à Kyiv, a déclaré mercredi une responsable des services de renseignement danois.
